en: Salutations to the glorious Gurus. The ritual for the *gulika* [time-unit] according to the teachings of Pīthupāda. For the placement (*nyāsa*) of Mṛtyuñjaya:
one should perform the sprinkling with the root mantra upon the hair-tuft (*keśola*). To the deity: Oṃ hoi yāghaḍacāśalaṃkha-thane.
Veda || Oṃ ājighra || Oṃ pañcanadya || Oṃ imam me || Oṃ sitāsita || Oṃ upahvare || Oṃ ye tīrthāni ||

With the root mantra, [perform] three *añjali* gestures. With the root mantra, perform the recitation (*japa*). (3) [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth, up to the *dhenumudrā*. With "Ho Ho Ya" and so forth, and with the *laṃkhana* mantra, [perform] the bathing of the deity. Oṃ, may he grant us well-being. Oṃ, the loudly roaring one. [Perform] the five-nectar bath (*pañcāmṛtasnāna*). [Recite] the Veda. Oṃ.

*Payapṛthivī* || *Dadhikrāvṇaḥ* || *Oṃ tejo 'si* || *Oṃ madhu vātā* || *Oṃ namaḥ śa*** || *Oṃ āśuśiśānaḥ* || *Oṃ yaj jāgrataḥ* || *Oṃ sahasraśrī*** || *Oho yāghara-cāśacoṅa laṃkhana devasnāna*** || (*Oṃ svasti no mimītā*)

|| Oṃ Dadhikrāvan || Bath with the Five Nectars (Pañcāmṛta-snāna) || Veda || Oṃ *payas pṛthivyām* || Oṃ *dadhikrāvṇo* || Oṃ *tejo'si* || Oṃ *madhu vātā* || Oṃ *namaḥ śambhavāya* || Oṃ *āśuśiśāno* || Oṃ *yaj jāgrataḥ* || Oṃ *sahasraśīrṣā* ||
Oṃ, may Indra grant us well-being. Oṃ, [may] Viṣṇu’s [gifts] come to us. Oṃ, homage to Śambhu. Oho-yā-kholā-na.
Oṃ, those who are the sacred fords (tīrthas). Oho-sā-arghā-na. Oṃ, the final ablution (avabhṛtha). Lūṃ, yā-khvalā-na. Oṃ, and the bond of Varuṇa.

Śaṅkha (**). Oṃ pavitreṣṭho. Oṃ tasyato. Oṃ śrīścate. Oṃ dyo śā (***). Oṃ vibhrāta. Oṃ namaste. Oṃ vaya ṭhaṃ (8). Oṃ sva śrī gurave (5). Devatha (***). Saṃtaya. Ceta. Yadadyaga (**). Hā (*). A (**). Oṃ (*).

Kṣaṃ Namaḥ. Oṃ Jave Śa Jāno. Oṃ Ta Yu. Oṃ Phalanī. Devayā Deguliyaṅahaya Kotosasa Sūryya. Sūryya-pūjā. Having performed the ritual rinsing of the mouth (ācamana) with the threefold truth (tritatva), perform the preliminary worship (thāpūjā) and offer the water for the libation (argha) to the Sun.

Nityāyāmumāla: Nyāsa for Sūrya; offering of the *argha* vessel; the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) ritual; invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth; the lotus gesture (*padmamudrā*); the worship of Ā; the offering of the seat; [worship] of Sūrya; the triple *añjali*; (3) Gāyatrī; [worship] of Āditya and others; the six-limbed ritual; invocation and so forth; the *bali* offering; Oṃ.
Accept this offering (*bali*), svāhā! Incense, lamp, and this food offering (*naivedya*).
Japa: *hrāṃ svāhā*. (10) Praise (*stotra*).
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Sūrya. I am Bhāratī; I am a sinner. Herein [are offered] perfumes and other articles. May this worship of Śrī Sūrya be entirely complete.
Now follows the worship of Viṣṇu.
Having sipped water (ācamana), [perform] the salutation to the Gurus. Oṃ, [salutation] to the lotus-face of the Lord Vāsudeva. [Perform] the ritual placement (nyāsa). [Salutation] to Viṣṇu.
The worship of the arghya vessel for Viṣṇu with the six limbs.

The invocation and so forth are performed with the conch mudrā. Self-worship (*ātmapūjā*). At the arrangement of the six doors: *Oṃ gaṇapataye* (2) *ḥ*. *Oṃ gurubhyaḥ* (2) *ḥ*. *Oṃ nandine* (2) *ḥ*. *Oṃ bhṛṅgi* (**) *ḥ*. *Oṃ dvārapālāya* (2) *ḥ*. *Oṃ kṣetrapālāya* (2) *ḥ*. Invocation and so forth. At the arrangement of the seats, [worship] Viṣṇu.

[The ritual for] Śrīguḷe Viṣṇu: the Gāyatrī of Brahmā; the worship of Keśava and others; the worship of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga); the invocation (āvāhana) and other rites; incense (dhūpa); lamp (dīpa); this food offering (naivedya), obeisance! To the three deities at the western door, the bali offering: Oṃ Hrīṃ Viṣvaksena; Oṃ Hrīṃ Hsauṃ Jayāvaha.
Oṃ śauṃ hrīṃ aiṃ haraṇakaraṇe. Japastotra: Oṃ, salutations to the Blessed One Vāsudeva. Salutations to Ananta.

"I am a sinner. Here [are offered] perfumes and so forth, according to the ritual for the worship of Viṣṇu. Then follows the worship of the eyes. Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana):
Nyāsa, Mūlana, Arghapātra [***], Ṣaḍaṅga, Ātmapūjā, Āsana [**], extending the three añjalis, Gāyatrī, Oṃ Juṃ Saḥ Amṛtī [***], Sadyojāta and other pūjās,
Ṣaḍaṅga, Āvāhana and others [(*), Po [2] Dīpo [2] Idaṃ Naivedyaṃ [2]], Bali, Dathupātasa.
Trideva || Oṃ juṃ Rudra-mātṛ-gaṇa || Oṃ juṃ Indra-Agni || Japa || Sohmāsaṃḍathehayāya ||

The Root Ritual of the Worship of Mṛtyuñjaya. Having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*) and the ritual placement of mantras (*nyāsa*), [one performs] the worship of the vessel of offering (*arghapātra*). [This is for] the seat of the *praṇava* (OM).
To the embodiment of the Praṇava, (2) ḥ. To the Praṇava, (2) ḥ.
One should visualize the Dhātrī, the Milk Ocean, a lotus, and the radiant orb of the moon;
thereafter, one should sprinkle [the image] with nectar arising from a portion of Time (kālakalā).
The six-limbed [rite] (ṣaḍaṅga); the invocation and so forth (āvāhanādi); the cow-mudrā (dhenumudrā); purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhiḥ); Oṃ juṃ hloṃ, the kalā of cessation (nivṛttikalā).
On the forehead: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, [homage] to the Great Bhairava of Nectar. Self-worship. The seat.
Oṃ juṃ to Dharma (2) ḥ || Oṃ juṃ to Jñāna (2) ḥ || Oṃ juṃ to Vairāgya (2) ḥ || Oṃ juṃ to Aiśvarya (2) ḥ || Oṃ juṃ to Adharma (2) ḥ ||
Oṃ juṃ to ignorance: ḥ || Oṃ juṃ to lack of dispassion: ḥ || Oṃ juṃ to lack of sovereignty: ḥ ||
Oṃ juṃ to Adhaśchanda, svāhā. Oṃ juṃ to Ūrdhvacchanda, svāhā. Oṃ juṃ to Ādhāraśakti, and so forth. [Meditation:
Oṃ juṃ, [I meditate upon Him] who resembles pure crystal, like the *kunda* flower or snow.
And she was adorned with necklaces decorated with cool sandalwood paste.
Soma is situated within the heart, with one face and three eyes,
resembling the full moon and as radiant as a mass of rays.
In her right hands she holds a water-pot, and in her left, upon a moon-maṇḍala;
the goddess has gone to the left thigh [of the deity], who is one-faced and three-eyed.
The goddess is white in color, greatly radiant, bestowing the boons of granting wishes and fearlessness;
she holds a conch and a lotus, and is the granter of all desires.
The Great God Mṛtyuñjaya, Amṛteśvarabhairava.
And meditating thus, I [strive] for the destruction of all evils.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, to Mṛtyuñjaya, this flower of meditative concentration (2) ḥ.
The triple añjali; the Gāyatrī; Oṃ (**), to Amṛtīśa; the worship of Sadyojāta and the others; the worship of Brahmā (**).
The worship of Asitāṅga and the others; the invocation and subsequent rites.
(****) This is the lamp (2); this is the food offering (2). (***): To Rudra and the host of Mothers, together with the *dathupāta* offering.

Oṃ Juṃ Indra Agni. The mantra for the invocation of the eastern quarter. To the Three Deities: Ha-kāra, Sa-kāra, Sa-kāra, Ha-kāra. Offering (*bali*). Aiṃ Hsphrīṃ Kubjikā. Shake the great *bali* of the self-offering.
Incense, Lamp, Food Offering, Consecration, Recitation, and Praise.
Oṃ! For our auspiciousness! Oṃkāra-bindu! Pure and peaceful! Homage be to you! I am a sinner!
Herein: the offering of fragrance and so forth; the Vedic worship. *Oṃ ā kṛṣṇe*; *Oṃ viṣṇorarāṭa*; *Oṃ śrīścate*; *Oṃ pāvakā naḥ*; *Oṃ namo vāyave*; *Oṃ i mande vā*; *Oṃ śrīścate*.
May this entire Vedic worship be completely fulfilled. O Sadāśiva, conqueror of death, may the limbs of the Vedas never abandon us.
Salutations again and again to Sarvaśānti, for the destruction of all evils.
(***) || Heramba-pūjā || For the purpose of drawing [the mandala] || Oṃ Deva (***) || Ceta || Oṃ Yadadyaga ||
Flower: Oṃ yāḥ phalinī. Having sipped water (ācamana), [perform] the ritual placement (nyāsa) and the worship of the argha vessel with the six-limbed [mantra].
The Cow; Self-Worship; the vessel for the bali offering; the Three Deities; the Veda; Oṃ *gaṇānāṃ tvā*; Oṃ *jātavedase*; Oṃ *imā rudrāya*.
Oṃ ghṛtaṃ ghṛta || Oṃ namo varuṇāya || Oṃ asaṃkhyātā ||
Āsana: Tryañjali: Aiṃ kroṃ gluṃ hrīṃ gluṃ kloṃ hrīṃ namaḥ (3). Hrīṃ gluṃ, to Cañcalādevī together with Śakti (*). Bali: Glāṃ glīṃ glūṃ gleṃḥ glauṃ haṃ (9), to Heramba (9) [and] Devī.

The six-limbed [rite] (*ṣaḍaṅga*); the sequence beginning with invocation (*āvāhanādi*); the elephant-mudrā (*gajamudrā*); the Vaiṣṇava-nyāsa; the shadow of the three-fold añjali-gesture of Lakṣmī; *hmaṃ* (three times); Garuḍa: *oṃ hrīṃ garuḍātmane* (twice) *ḥ*; the sequence beginning with invocation; the *thā-thu-vā-pā-sa* [mantra]; the Sūrya-nyāsa.
Three *añjali*s for Viṣṇu-nyāsa; three *añjali*s for Ananta-skanda; the rites beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth; three *añjali*s for Kumāra-skanda.
Oṃ kuṃ, to Kumāra: [mudrā] with three añjalis and the bull. Oṃ, to Vṛṣabha: [mudrā] with three añjalis. [Mudrā] with three añjalis for Umā and Maheśvara together.

The Mahāmṛtyuñjaya-nyāsa: The three-fold añjali for Mṛtyuñjaya; The three-fold añjali for the sword-bearer (Paṭṭisa) Mṛtyuñjaya; The three-fold añjali for the door-guardian; The three-fold añjali for the root of the field (Kṣetramūla); The offering of bali, incense, lamp, and food (naivedya).
(***) Tra || Fair-complexioned, three-eyed || Homage to Ananta || (**) Peaceful || Just as an arrow ||
Here [are the mantras for] the offering of fragrance and so forth, and the worship of the feet: Oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā... Oṃ dyāṃ māle... Oṃ viṣṇorarāṭa...
Oṃ pāvakā naḥ... Oṃ idaṃ viṣṇu... Oṃ sahasraśīrṣā... Oṃ suparṇo 'si...

Oṃ ākṛṣṇe || Oṃ tanmitrasya || Oṃ yatra bāṇā || Oṃ āśuḥ śiśā || Oṃ namaḥ śaṃ || Oṃ dyāṃ māle || Oṃ vayaḥ soma || Oṃ atastvaṃ deva || Vedārccana || (*). The ritual for the day of Aṅgāra (Tuesday) and the Kuhu new moon. Baline ghā (**). Together with the Veda of the Devas. Herambasa.
Āsa [with] añjali; bali with the six limbs; invocation and so forth; gaja [with] mahābali, shaking it.

Incense, lamps, recitation (japa), and hymns (stotra). For the recitation: hymns; here [the rites] beginning with Gaṅgā; Vedic worship; *oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā*; *oṃ dyāṃ mā le*; the offering of bali; three handfuls of water (*añjali*) for the Sun and other deities; recitation (japa) and hymns (stotra).
Thus concludes the *sthāpūjā*. Then the patron (*yajamāna*) offers three handfuls of water (*añjali*).
[This is followed by] incense, lamps, recitation (*jāpa*), hymns (*stotra*), Vedic worship (*vedārccana*), and the circle of deities (*devatucakra*).

The procedure for the sacrificer’s departure, the consecration, the *svānaviya*, the *devasucuke*, the *nyāsalikāya*, and the *lakotryalichāya*—these constitute the daily ritual for the ancestors. This is the procedure for the recitation of Śanaiścara.
(**) Sandalwood, sacred thread, and flowers; (***) the Veda-knowledge; (*1) the *sa* syllable; the worship of the *argha* vessel.
Self-worship. Bali for the three deities. Veda: Oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā... [etc. 5. Seat.
The powers of the support (*ādhāraśakti*) and so forth; [the mantra] for Gṛdhrāsana: *ḥ*; the three-fold *añjali* offering; the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*).
The rites beginning with the invocation (āvāhana).
Oṃ śrā śri śru śmlvryū, homage to Śanaiścara Mahābhairava.
[Mudrā] || Oṃ śanno devī || Oṃ yamena dattaṃ || Cekanaluya || Oṃ prajāpate || Bali || Oṃ aghore hrāṃ paramaghore ghorāmukhi vama (2) piba (2) ru (2) rajamurttaye baliṃ.
Gṛhṇa svāhā! To Mahābalin Dhunaka: for the recitation of incense, lamps, mantra-repetition, and hymns of praise.
Hymn: Oṃ, may the heavens be peaceful. This is the *balithvaya*. [Thus ends the recitation of Śanaiścara.]
Auspiciousness.
